content.text:
I've submitted **index 4 (Nb 0.456, V 0.544)** as the best composition. It had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, **8.56 µA**.

The library is a Nb–V oxide line running from about 46% to 71% Nb, with 16 candidates. I had 3 photocurrent measurements and used all of them. I used 4 of the 5 XRD scans.

- **XRD:** a mixed Nb–V oxide phase shows up in samples from 46% to 62% Nb and gives its strongest signal near a 1:1 ratio (index 11). At 71% Nb (index 13) that phase is gone and a different one appears. The strongest peaks are the same in every sample, so they are probably from the substrate.
- **Photocurrent:**

  | Index | Nb fraction | Photocurrent |
  |---|---|---|
  | 13 | 0.714 | −3.17 µA |
  | 11 | 0.505 | 6.26 µA |
  | 4 | 0.456 | 8.56 µA |

Photocurrent rose steadily as vanadium increased, so I spent the last measurement on index 4, the most vanadium-rich candidate. The best composition probably sits at or near that end of the library. I can't rule out the unmeasured middle compositions (roughly 55–65% Nb), but on this trend they should fall between index 13 and index 11.
